title: Water Security Financing Framework for Latin America and the Caribbean
summary: ECLAC presents a practical framework for turning water-security needs into bankable investment programmes amid climate, urbanization, and fiscal pressures. It covers project appraisal, institutional design, green and blue bonds, blended finance, climate funds, and other mechanisms for mobilizing public and private capital.

title: Digital and Sustainable Trade Facilitation in Latin America and the Caribbean: Regional Report 2025
summary: ECLAC reports that the region implemented 73% of the core measures in the 2025 UN Global Survey on Digital and Sustainable Trade Facilitation, slightly above the global average and 5.9 percentage points above 2023. Progress was led by paperless and cross-border digital trade measures, but greater subregional coordination remains a priority.

title: St. Vincent and the Grenadines: 2026 Article IV Consultation — Staff Report
summary: The IMF finds that repeated external shocks have widened fiscal deficits and pushed public debt to unsustainable levels. The report focuses on restoring fiscal sustainability while addressing high living costs, weak growth, and financial-sector vulnerabilities.

title: Barbados: 2026 Article IV Consultation and Request for a Stand-By Arrangement — Staff Report
summary: The IMF credits the BERT programme with strengthening macroeconomic stability, rebuilding reserves, and putting public debt on a downward path. It also reviews the authorities' request for a precautionary Stand-By Arrangement and the next phase of fiscal and climate-resilience reforms.

title: CDB Annual Report 2025
summary: CDB reports US$464.6 million in project approvals during 2025 and reviews its investments in infrastructure, climate action, education, and private-sector development across its borrowing members. The report also covers the Bank's financial performance, resource mobilization, risk management, and audited statements.

title: Trinidad and Tobago: 2026 Article IV Consultation — Staff Report
summary: The IMF finds a slow recovery supported by non-energy activity, low inflation, and a sound banking system, but notes weaker external and fiscal positions as energy revenues decline. It recommends fiscal consolidation, measures to stem capital outflows, and a gradual move toward greater exchange-rate flexibility.

title: Antigua and Barbuda: 2026 Article IV Consultation — Staff Report
summary: The IMF reports continued economic expansion and easing inflation, alongside a decline in the public-debt ratio from its pandemic peak. Significant arrears, high financing needs, and weaker Citizenship-by-Investment revenue remain central fiscal risks.

title: St. Kitts and Nevis: 2026 Article IV Consultation — Staff Report
summary: The IMF expects growth to recover in 2026, but warns that lower Citizenship-by-Investment revenue, large fiscal and current-account deficits, and reduced buffers constrain the policy response to shocks. It calls for continued fiscal consolidation, stronger fiscal rules, renewable-energy investment, and labour-market reforms.

title: Caribbean Economic Review and Outlook 2025–2026
summary: CDB estimates that regional growth excluding Guyana slowed to 0.6% in 2025 and projects a modest recovery to 1.1% in 2026. The report examines growth, inflation, fiscal and debt performance, external balances, financial stability, and the implementation deficits constraining long-run development.

title: Regional Economic Outlook for the Western Hemisphere, April 2026
summary: The IMF assesses the Western Hemisphere's exposure to the 2026 energy and food-price shock, distinguishing gains for large oil exporters from the pressures facing import-dependent economies with high debt or limited reserves. It argues for targeted support to vulnerable households while preserving scarce fiscal space.

title: World Economic Outlook, April 2026: Global Economy in the Shadow of War
summary: The IMF projects global growth of 3.1% in 2026 under an assumption of a limited Middle East conflict, with inflation temporarily rising before resuming its decline. The report emphasizes downside risks from prolonged conflict, fragmentation, trade tensions, and already-thin policy buffers.

title: Slow Growth in Latin America and the Caribbean amid Global Uncertainty and Weak Investment
summary: The World Bank projects Latin America and the Caribbean to grow 2.1% in 2026 as high borrowing costs, weak external demand, and uncertainty weigh on investment and job creation. It argues that skills, finance, trade integration, and institutional capacity are prerequisites for productivity-enhancing industrial policy.

title: Economic Survey of Latin America and the Caribbean, 2025: Resource Mobilization to Finance Development
summary: ECLAC combines its regional macroeconomic outlook with an assessment of the fiscal, structural, and institutional constraints on development finance. It examines domestic resource mobilization, private finance, international financial architecture, and the role of development banks in productive transformation.

title: Statistical Yearbook for Latin America and the Caribbean, 2025
summary: ECLAC's bilingual yearbook compiles internationally comparable economic, social, demographic, and environmental indicators for the region. The 2025 edition includes national accounts, external-sector and price statistics, and highlights the large difference between Caribbean growth with and without Guyana.

title: The Bahamas: 2025 Article IV Consultation — Staff Report
summary: The IMF finds that tourism and construction have supported a solid recovery and improving fiscal balances, while public debt remains elevated. Priorities include additional fiscal measures, stronger public-sector and financial reporting, electricity reform, and greater resilience to natural disasters.

title: Suriname: 2025 Article IV Consultation — Staff Report
summary: The IMF says Suriname must rebuild fiscal and monetary discipline while preparing institutions to manage a prospective oil boom. It warns that policy slippages in 2025 raised inflation and weakened the currency, despite strong gold prices and an improved medium-term resource outlook.

title: Grenada: 2025 Article IV Consultation — Staff Report
summary: The IMF finds Grenada's economy resilient after Hurricane Beryl, supported by reconstruction, investment, and tourism. Savings from Citizenship-by-Investment revenue and contingent financing have preserved fiscal space, though natural disasters, external demand, and large current-account deficits remain key risks.

title: Preliminary Overview of the Economies of the Caribbean 2023–2024
summary: ECLAC compares growth, employment, monetary conditions, fiscal and external accounts across the Caribbean and includes briefs for The Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Guyana, Jamaica, Suriname, Trinidad and Tobago, and the Eastern Caribbean Currency Union. It provides a compact subregional counterpart to ECLAC's wider Latin America and Caribbean outlook.

title: Kingdom of the Netherlands—Aruba: 2025 Article IV Consultation Discussions — Staff Report
summary: The IMF reports strong tourism-led growth, improved fiscal balances, and a declining debt ratio after the pandemic. It recommends continued adherence to the fiscal framework, measures to reduce living costs, and reforms that raise productivity, resilience, and the efficiency of public spending.

title: Belize: 2025 Article IV Consultation — Staff Report
summary: The IMF expects growth to settle near 2% as tourism reaches capacity constraints and commodity prices ease. It calls for additional fiscal consolidation, better access to finance, structural reforms, and stronger resilience to natural disasters to keep debt declining.

title: Kingdom of the Netherlands—Curaçao and Sint Maarten: 2025 Article IV Consultation Discussions — Staff Report
summary: The IMF finds that tourism and construction continued to drive strong growth in Curaçao and Sint Maarten, while fiscal positions remained in surplus and the monetary union stayed broadly sound. It recommends renewed momentum on tax, investment-management, labour-market, and other structural reforms.

title: Jamaica: 2025 Article IV Consultation — Staff Report
summary: The IMF credits Jamaica's fiscal, monetary, and institutional reforms with increasing resilience to shocks, but identifies low productivity and persistent supply-side constraints as barriers to faster growth. Recommended reforms include a clearer debt anchor, stronger monetary transmission, deeper foreign-exchange markets, and continued financial-stability work.

title: Dominica: 2025 Article IV Consultation — Staff Report
summary: The IMF projects continued growth from tourism and development investment, but warns that public debt remains high and disaster risks are substantial. It recommends stronger fiscal consolidation, better financial-sector oversight, and institutional reforms to improve policy execution and resilient growth.

title: Guyana: 2025 Article IV Consultation — Staff Report
summary: The IMF describes an exceptionally strong outlook driven by rapidly expanding oil production, robust non-oil activity, and major public investment. It stresses that a medium-term fiscal framework, strong governance of resource wealth, and close monitoring of inflation and absorptive capacity are essential for inclusive and stable growth.

title: St. Lucia: 2024 Article IV Consultation — Staff Report
summary: The IMF finds that tourism, construction, and manufacturing completed St. Lucia's post-pandemic recovery, but expects growth to slow as major projects mature. High debt rollover needs, investment delays, climate exposure, and limited fiscal space remain the principal risks.

title: Haiti: 2024 Article IV Consultation — Staff Report
summary: The IMF assesses Haiti's outlook as exceptionally uncertain amid overlapping security, humanitarian, social, and economic crises. The report prioritizes zero monetary financing of the budget, stronger revenue and expenditure controls, protection of social spending, and more timely and transparent economic data.
